findings.name: Three parallel storylines
findings.detail: The overworld unlocks three player-orderable storylines after a short prologue: 'Victory Road' (Gym Challenge, 8 Gym Leaders), 'Path of Legends' (5 Titan Pokémon with Arven), and '★ Starfall Street ★' (5 Team Star bases). The player can tackle them in any order, in any mixture, at their own pace.
findings.trackable: Progress on each path is tracked in the game's menu/map via badge icons, Titan defeat markers, and Team Star base icons turning gray once cleared.

findings.name: Prologue / Treasure Hunt assignment
findings.detail: Player moves to Cabo Poco in Paldea with their mother, attends Naranja Academy (Scarlet) / Uva Academy (Violet), receives starter Pokémon from Director Clavell, meets Nemona (student council president) and Arven, rescues/is rescued by a wounded Koraidon (Scarlet) that later becomes the Legendary partner, receives the Tera Orb, and is given the 'Treasure Hunt' independent-study assignment by Clavell that formally unlocks all three storylines.
findings.trackable: Story progression; not itself counted numerically.

findings.name: Klawf — Stony Cliff Titan
findings.detail: Located in South Province (Area Three). Multi-phase fight: player battles alone first, Titan flees/regroups, then a second-phase battle occurs with Arven assisting.
findings.trackable: Path of Legends progress in the map/menu; Herba Mystica added to inventory.

findings.trackable: Path of Legends progress in the map/menu; Herba Mystica added to inventory.

findings.name: Great Tusk — Quaking Earth Titan (SCARLET EXCLUSIVE FORM)
findings.detail: Located in Asado Desert. In Pokémon Scarlet this Titan is Great Tusk; the Violet-version equivalent is Iron Treads. This is a direct version-exclusive difference in the Path of Legends questline.
findings.trackable: Path of Legends progress in the map/menu; Herba Mystica added to inventory.

findings.name: Tatsugiri — False Dragon Titan
findings.detail: Located at Casseroya Lake; the true Titan is Tatsugiri, though the much larger Dondozo it rides also appears in the fight (Dondozo is not itself the Titan). This is the final/climactic Titan battle before Arven's full-power battle.
findings.trackable: Path of Legends progress in the map/menu; Herba Mystica added to inventory.

findings.name: Arven (Path of Legends finale)
findings.detail: After all 5 Titans are defeated and enough Herba Mystica are collected, the Path of Legends climaxes in a full-strength Pokémon battle against Arven, whose partner Mabosstiff needed the Herba Mystica-based medicine.
findings.trackable: Marks completion of the Path of Legends storyline.

findings.name: Penny (as 'Cassiopeia', Starfall Street finale)
findings.detail: Penny is the true 'Big Boss' of Team Star, operating under the online alias 'Cassiopeia.' Backstory: Team Star originated from bullied students who confronted their tormentors; after a scandal, Penny/Cassiopeia took sole responsibility and studied abroad, leaving the five squad bosses to run the team in her absence. After all 5 bases are cleared, Penny reveals herself as Cassiopeia and battles the player to formally announce Team Star's disbanding.
findings.trackable: Marks completion of the Starfall Street storyline.

findings.name: Arven
findings.detail: Companion NPC who requests help defeating the 5 Titans for Herba Mystica to heal his Mabosstiff; later revealed to be the son of the deceased Professor Sada.

findings.name: Nemona
findings.detail: Paldea Academy student council president and a Champion-level trainer; recurring rival/support character across the story, battled repeatedly.

findings.name: Penny
findings.detail: True leader of Team Star under the alias 'Cassiopeia'; initially presented as a reclusive, harassed student.

findings.name: Professor Sada (AI) — SCARLET VERSION NAME
findings.detail: The 'professor' character who guides the player throughout the game is an AI construct modeled on the real Professor Sada, who died 10 years prior. In Pokémon Scarlet this character/AI is named Sada; the Violet-version equivalent is named Turo. The real Sada obsessively researched Paradox Pokémon from the past via a time machine in Area Zero and died protecting a passive Koraidon from a more aggressive, territorial one.

findings.name: No character named 'Clive' exists in Pokémon Scarlet/Violet
findings.detail: Searched confirmed there is no 'Clive' in the game. The AI professor is named Sada (Scarlet) / Turo (Violet). The academy director is named Clavell (Bug/Steel-toned similarity to 'Clive' may be the source of confusion). Flagging this so downstream trophy text does not reference a nonexistent character.

findings.name: Director Clavell
findings.detail: Director of Naranja Academy (Scarlet) / Uva Academy (Violet); gives the player their starter Pokémon and formally issues the 'Treasure Hunt' assignment that opens up the three storylines.

findings.name: The Way Home (Area Zero climax)
findings.detail: The fourth/final narrative chapter, unlocked after completing all three paths (Victory Road, Path of Legends, Starfall Street). The full group descends into the Great Crater of Paldea / Area Zero to reach the Zero Lab. Inside, the player proceeds alone while companions hold off Paradox Pokémon outside. The AI professor reveals it is a robot built on the real Sada/Turo's research; the player must defeat the AI in a Pokémon battle, then confront and defeat the second, hostile Koraidon/Miraidon (the one that killed the real professor) in a final wild Pokémon battle.
findings.trackable: Story/credits milestone; no separate numeric counter.

findings.name: Single ending — Paradise Protection Protocol
findings.detail: After the final battle, a 'Paradise Protection Protocol' activates; the AI chooses to travel to another era via the time machine, allowing it to be shut down permanently and preventing further Paradox Pokémon leaking into Paldea. The game concludes with the player and friends taking 'a slow and scenic route back to Mesagoza,' then returning to normal academy life. No branching endings were found — this is a single, fixed ending for the base game (DLC provides additional post-credits story content, see below).

findings.name: Koraidon — Scarlet-exclusive Legendary/cover Pokémon
findings.detail: Koraidon is the box-art Legendary and player's companion throughout Pokémon Scarlet, described as a 'primeval'-themed form; its Paradox Pokémon (ancient-past themed) are the version-exclusive Paradox species found throughout Scarlet. The Violet-exclusive equivalent is Miraidon (mechanical/future-themed) with future-themed Paradox Pokémon.

findings.name: Academy Ace Tournament
findings.detail: A post-game repeatable tournament activity available after completing the main story, featuring rebattles against notable NPCs/rivals in a bracket format.
findings.trackable: Uncertain — could not confirm an in-game completion tracker for tournament wins/rank beyond story flags.

findings.name: The Teal Mask (DLC Part 1 — The Hidden Treasure of Area Zero)
findings.detail: Set in Kitakami, a new region reached via Naranja/Uva Academy's school trip. Key characters: Briar (Blueberry Academy teacher, descendant of a character named Heath, possesses an uncensored 'Scarlet Book'/'Violet Book' manuscript), Carmine and Kieran (local siblings, Blueberry Academy students), their grandparents Yukito and Hideko, and photographer Perrin. Story centers on the legendary Ogerpon and the 'Loyal Three' (Okidogi, Munkidori, Fezandipiti), who must be defeated to retrieve Ogerpon's masks, followed by a final battle against Kieran and the capture of Ogerpon. Story content does not differ between Scarlet and Violet versions.

findings.name: The Indigo Disk (DLC Part 2 — The Hidden Treasure of Area Zero)
findings.detail: Set at Blueberry Academy in a Terarium (an artificial undersea dome with four biomes) located within the Unova region. Key characters: Cyrano (academy director), Kieran (now a rival who becomes the BB League Champion), Carmine, and Briar, plus returning base-game characters Geeta and Rika. The BB League's four Elite Four-equivalents are Lacey, Crispin, Amarys, and Drayton, each with a unique challenge/trial type; after defeating all four, the player faces Kieran as Champion. The climax occurs in an area called Area Zero Underdepths. Post-game unlocks access to 25 Legendary Pokémon from past generations via Blueberry Quests and special snacks, encountered within Paldea. Story content does not differ between Scarlet and Violet versions.

Path of Legends progress shown on the region map (icons change once a Titan is cleared); Herba Mystica appear as inventory items.
Rotom Phone Pokédex app tracks Seen/Caught counts. Paldea Pokédex contains 400 entries in the base game (numbered 001–400); DLC (Kitakami + Blueberry) adds further entries to a combined Pokédex.

Story/credits flag; per Serebii, the Elite Four sequence can only be challenged once during the main story push (rematches likely available later via League Club or Academy Ace Tournament, not independently confirmed).

versionNotes.note: Koraidon (primeval-themed) is the Scarlet-exclusive cover Legendary and player companion; Miraidon (futuristic-themed) is the Violet equivalent. This affects which Paradox Pokémon (past- vs future-themed) populate each version.
The Path of Legends 'Quaking Earth Titan' is Great Tusk in Scarlet and Iron Treads in Violet — a direct version-exclusive difference within a mandatory campaign boss fight.
The AI-professor character central to the main plot is named Sada in Scarlet and Turo in Violet.
The academy attended by the player is Naranja Academy in Scarlet and Uva Academy in Violet (cosmetic/name difference, same story role).

Could not confirm any other Scarlet-exclusive story beats, side characters, or additional Scarlet-only campaign content beyond the Koraidon/Sada/Great Tusk/Naranja Academy naming differences noted above. Best available information suggests the core campaign structure (paths, bosses, ending) is otherwise identical between Scarlet and Violet.
